messages:
maria: Quick sanity check — for per-org bursts do we charge against SKU buckets or plan-tier buckets? thinking small/medium/large SKUs at the edge to keep metrics simple.
kevin: leaning SKU mapping. clearer billing metric. but must avoid double-counting when an org has multiple keys.
sophie: +1 SKU. propose: assign a sku label to each API key at creation; bursts consume from key SKU bucket, but org-level reserve is checked first.
maria: that handles per-key vs per-org. if org has reserved capacity, bursts pull from org pool; otherwise fallback to key SKU.
austin: need audit trail. when key consumes org pool, tag metrics with org_id and key_id. billing: reserved-bucket consumption billed at commit rate; burst overage billed at SKU on-demand rate.
kevin: UX ask: console should show 'reserved vs burst' meter per org and per key. also surface last-burst timestamp and charge estimate. quota-bot: please add alert suggestions. :eyes: 
quota-bot: [auto] alert rule created: burst_exceed -> notify #billing when burst >= 80% for 10m.
sophie: config sketch:
```
quota_policy:
  assign_on_create:
    sku: PRO
  org_pool: true
  fallback: sku-burst
```
maria: implementation note: routing check order = org_pool -> key_sku_pool -> fallback_sku_pool. avoid race on decrement: use token-bucket CAS on edge cache (redis lua or etcd txn).
austin: also set plan-specific burst windows: free = 10s sliding, pro = 60s, ent = 5m. reduces abuse and aligns cost.
kevin: agreed. next steps: sophie to draft RFC for edge mapping + console mocks; austin to spec billing tags/event schema. target: EOD Fri for initial sync. :+1:
